title: Stalks commute with total tensor products of sheaf complexes
statement: Let $(X,\mathcal O_X)$ be a ringed space, let $F^\bullet$ and $K^\bullet$ be complexes of sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules], and let $x\in X$. There is a natural isomorphism of complexes of $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-modules $(F^\bullet\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}K^\bullet)_x \cong F_x^\bullet\otimes_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}K_x^\bullet$ for the total tensor construction [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], where both sides use the total-complex direct sums and tensor differential.

source.place: Cohomology, Lemma Tag 06YB (label lemma-check-K-flat-stalks), tensor-stalk identification

proof.text: For each integer $n$, the degree-$n$ term of the total tensor complex is $\bigoplus_{p+q=n}\mathcal F^p\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal K^q$ by [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Applying [lem-pc-stalk-direct-sums] to this coproduct gives a canonical identification of its stalk with $\bigoplus_{p+q=n}(\mathcal F^p\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal K^q)_x$.

source.place: Cohomology, Lemma Tag 06YB (label lemma-check-K-flat-stalks), tensor-stalk identification

proof.text: For every pair $(p,q)$, the canonical module-stalk comparison [lem-pc-ringed-space-module-stalk-tensor] gives $(\mathcal F^p\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal K^q)_x\cong\mathcal F_x^p\otimes_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}\mathcal K_x^q$, naturally in both module sheaves. Taking the direct sum of these component isomorphisms identifies the degree-$n$ term with $\bigoplus_{p+q=n}\mathcal F_x^p\otimes_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}\mathcal K_x^q$.

source.place: Cohomology, Lemma Tag 06YB (label lemma-check-K-flat-stalks), tensor-stalk identification; Modules, Lemma Tag 01CB

proof.text: The comparisons in the preceding steps carry each summand's tensor differential to the corresponding stalk tensor differential, because the module comparison [lem-pc-ringed-space-module-stalk-tensor] is natural and the stalk map sends a germ of a section to the germ of its image. They therefore commute with the total differential $d_{\mathcal F}\otimes1+(-1)^p1\otimes d_{\mathcal K}$, with the same sign on both sides by [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Thus the degreewise maps assemble to the asserted natural isomorphism of complexes.
